To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the large firms of the late nineteenth century did not have a cost advantage in production, but that their cost advantage in marketing was substantial, and that this marketing advantage was the key to their success.

the rise of large scale production and the concomitant concentration in many industries was the result of the development of mass production technologies that required large scale production, the development of a mass market for consumer goods, and the development of a national transportation network that allowed firms to exploit the economies of scale inherent in mass production technologies and the mass market.
the large-scale enterprise was not a natural development of American industry, but rather a product of deliberate and conscious efforts by business leaders.
